title: Research: sharpen the fixed P104 first-drop boundary to 54 copy cost
body:
For the exact PR1187 P104 decoder, two copy terms can drop at the same first boundary of 22 additional punctures. This improves its displayed 55-copy/82-port witness to 54 copies and proves 54 optimal there: 24 boundary cuts cost 54, 336 cost 55, and all others cost 56. A complete 1,792,252 cut-pair census, all 6,724 coefficient identities and single-port restoration controls support the fixed-decoder result. Its 54/82 ratio remains worse than 56/104; physical charges are unpriced.

Validation: Python 3.12 registered replay with source pins and scoped controls; selected-result integrity or baseline bindings and diff checks pass. See the [reproduction instructions, exact sources and remaining questions](https://github.com/woklerx/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0ebd49c31300e67698fd812fc00f2a3b2b805a67/research/p104-two-copy-drops/README.md). No selected source, certificate or kappa changes; no full selected circuit replay is claimed. Prepared by woklerx with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, with predecessor attribution retained.
